scenes.label: Brevio Studio
scenes.text: Brevio Studio turns one long lecture into a short, reviewed video, for the audience you choose.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.text: Lectures hold great ideas, but few people watch an hour of video. Cutting highlights by hand is slow, and fully automatic tools are hard to trust.

scenes.label: Step 1 · Source
scenes.text: You start with a lecture video and pick the audience: researchers, the general public, or kids. A source link is optional.

scenes.label: Step 2 · Clips
scenes.text: Brevio transcribes the lecture on your own computer and suggests the strongest clips. You keep up to five and fine tune each one.

scenes.label: Step 2 · Blueprint
scenes.text: Before writing anything, it plans the story: clip count, opening idea, bridges and ending. The finished video is checked against that plan.

scenes.label: Step 3 · Studio
scenes.text: It builds a preview with a narrated opening, bridges and ending, plus illustrations, music and captions, each section beside its source evidence.

scenes.label: Step 3 · Approval
scenes.text: Nothing is exported until a named reviewer has watched the preview and approved it.

scenes.label: Step 4 · Export
scenes.text: Every export gets two plain-language checks: technical, for media, captions and loudness, and structure, for order, bridges, narration and the plan.

scenes.label: Safeguards
scenes.text: Transcription, voices and rendering run locally. Only short text requests use the company gateway, capped at five per run. A person always decides.

scenes.label: Brevio Studio
scenes.text: Faster highlights, consistent quality, and a human in control. Try it on one lecture, and tell us what to improve.
